description: Keep a reverse SSH forward alive for as long as it is needed, and return the port P on that machine that reaches this computer's 127.0.0.1:D. A detached process holds it (it survives this process), re-establishes it when it drops, and keeps the same P while it can. Returns when the forward is ready (30 s, else SEAT_FORWARD_UNAVAILABLE). Call again before the next use: every call keeps it needed for 120 s more, and a session bound to the id keeps it needed. remote.ssh pins the host key file and one identity (paths only; the detached process restarts ssh by itself, so the agent socket must stay stable).

id.description: Opaque id of this forward (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, 1-64). The id of a registered terminal binding joins that binding's own forward.

remote.description: The machine to forward on: {host, user, port?, ssh: {known_hosts_file, host_key_alias?, identity_agent | identity_file}}. Required for an id that is not a terminal binding; ignored for one

remote_port.description: Ask for this port on that machine and never move to another (default: the machine's sshd picks one and it is kept)

to.description: Where the forward leads on this computer: 127.0.0.1 and the port D

name: ensure_forward
